title: Quotients by arbitrary closed subgroups and orbit identifications
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type, and all subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness, connectedness and morphism properties have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let $G$ be smooth and connected and let $H\subseteq G$ be any subgroup, not necessarily normal, smooth or connected. The fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/H(A)$, for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $F$-algebras, is represented by a separated finite-type $F$-scheme $G/H$. The canonical morphism $q:G\to G/H$ is faithfully flat and satisfies $q(gh)=q(g)$, and $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ is an isomorphism $G\times_F H\simeq G\times_{G/H}G$. For an action of $G$ on a separated finite-type $F$-scheme $X$ and $x\in X(F)$, the scheme-theoretic stabilizer $G_x$ has $G_x(A)=\{g:g x_A=x_A\}$. The orbit with its reduced structure is canonically isomorphic to $G/G_x$, by $gG_x\mapsto gx$. Every $F$-point of $G/H$ lifts to an $F$-point of $G$; thus $(G/H)(F)=G(F)/H(F)$.

source.place: Theorem 7.18, printed p.142; Propositions 5.24--5.25 and Corollary 5.27, pp.104--105; Propositions 7.11--7.12 and 7.17, pp.141--142.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-group-scheme-separated-field], $G$ is separated. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] with $k=F$ and $L=H$. Obtain a separated finite-type scheme $Y$ and a flat, surjective, finitely presented map $p:G\to Y$ such that, for every $F$-scheme $T$, $p(a)=p(b)$ if and only if $a^{-1}b\in H(T)$. In particular $p(gh)=p(g)$. No normality or reducedness of $H$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 5.28 and Definition 5.20, pp.104--105; Theorem 7.18, p.143; Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 047L, lemma-group-scheme-over-field-separated

proof.text: Use the coset criterion of [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] on $T=G\times_YG$, with its two universal projections $a,b$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is a unique morphism $h:T\to H$ with image $a^{-1}b$ in $G(T)$. Thus $(a,b)\mapsto(a,a^{-1}b)$ is a morphism $G\times_YG\to G\times_FH$. Its composites with $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ are the identities, since $g^{-1}(gh)=h$ and $a(a^{-1}b)=b$. This proves the torsor identity as an isomorphism of schemes.

The singleton $\{p\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. For $y:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$, pull it back by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] and apply [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement]. This gives finitely many affine schemes $V_j$ covering $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in the fppf topology and morphisms $V_j\to G$ lifting $y|_{V_j}$. Each $V_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally finitely presented, and is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since its source and target are affine. Thus these are the faithfully flat finitely presented affine coverings in the statement. If one uses singleton affine coverings instead, [lem-sfb-space-fppf-finite-affine-refinement] supplies a single affine flat surjective locally finitely presented refinement, which is finitely presented by the same permanence statement.

source.place: Proposition 5.7, p.99, affine-cover construction; Stacks topologies.tex Tags 021O (lemma-fppf), 021P (lemma-fppf-affine); schemes.tex Tags 03GI, 01KV

proof.text: Every represented functor is a sheaf for our coverings: [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] give precisely existence and uniqueness of gluing maps into $Y$. Put $P(A)=G(A)/H(A)$. The coset criterion in step 1 makes $P\to h_Y$ injective on each algebra, and step 3 makes every section of $h_Y$ locally a section of $P$. To check the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] explicitly, take any sheaf $E$ and map $P\to E$. For $y\in Y(A)$ choose the local lifts from step 3 and glue their images in $E$: on overlaps their cosets agree by step 1, so their images agree. Refining two choices shows independence; uniqueness of gluing proves naturality and uniqueness of the extension $h_Y\to E$. Hence $Y$ represents $P^\#$; write $G/H=Y$ and $q=p$.

source.place: Definition 5.20 and Proposition 5.21, p.104; Stacks topologies.tex Tag 022C; descent.tex Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms

proof.text: For an action on $X$ and $x\in X(F)$, form $G_x=G\times_{X\times_FX}X$, where $G\to X\times_FX$ is $g\mapsto(gx,x)$ and $X\to X\times_FX$ is the diagonal. Its $T$-points are exactly the $g$ with $gx_T=x_T$, by [def-pc-fibre-product]; the action identities make them a subgroup. Since $X$ is separated, its diagonal is closed, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) makes $G_x\hookrightarrow G$ closed. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry]: the reduced orbit $O_x$ is locally closed and smooth, and $a:G\to O_x$, $g\mapsto gx$, is faithfully flat. These conclusions allow nonreduced $X$ and nonreduced $G_x$.

source.place: Propositions 7.4 and 7.11--7.12, pp.139--142; Proposition 7.17, p.143; Stacks schemes.tex Tag 01KU, closed-immersion base change

proof.text: For completeness compare the schemes, rather than only their $F$-points. By [lem-trf-immersion-over-separated-base], the locally closed immersion $O_x\to X$ makes $O_x$ separated over $F$. The map $a:G\to O_x$ is finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target](b), since $G$ is finite type over $F$. Consequently $\{a\}$ is fpqc: it is flat, surjective and quasi-compact, which gives the finite affine subcover condition in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Likewise the quotient map $p_x:G\to Q_x=G/G_x$ from step 1 is fpqc. On $G\times_{Q_x}G$, the two orbit maps agree because $b=ah$ with $h\in G_x$; on $G\times_{O_x}G$, the two quotient maps agree because $ax=bx$ implies $(a^{-1}b)x=x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to descend these maps to $Q_x\to O_x$ and $O_x\to Q_x$, respectively. Their composites pull back to the identity on $G$; uniqueness in the same descent statement makes them inverse. The first map sends $gG_x$ to $gx$, so this is the claimed canonical orbit identification.

source.place: Propositions 7.11--7.12, pp.141--142; Definition 5.20 and Proposition 5.21, p.104; Stacks descent.tex Tag 023Q; Stacks schemes.tex Tag 01L8, lemma-subscheme-of-separated-scheme

proof.text: Let $y\in Y(F)$. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change], its fibre $Z=G\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}F$ is nonempty. It is of finite type over $F$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], applied to the finite-type map $p$ of step 1. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], closed points are dense in $Z$, hence there is a closed point $z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], $F\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism. Thus $z$ gives an $F$-point of the fibre, and its projection to $G$ lifts $y$. The fibre criterion of step 1 says that two such lifts differ by right multiplication by an element of $H(F)$, proving $Y(F)=G(F)/H(F)$. No smoothness of the fibre has been assumed.

Step 3 uses 021O(3) base change, 021P affine refinement, and affine source plus quasi-separated target plus lfp giving fp, with no Noetherian hypothesis. Step 4 is the sheafification universal property: P into h_Y is injective by the criterion and locally surjective by step 3, and gluing works through 022C fpqc and 023Q representable descent. lean.statement: theorem exists_homogeneous_fppf_quotient {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (G H : Over (Spec (.of F))) [GrpObj G] [GrpObj H] [IsAffine G.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] [Smooth G.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.left] [IsAffine H.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType H.hom] [QuasiCompact H.hom] (i : H ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] : ∃ (Q : Over (Spec (.of F))) (q : G ⟶ Q), IsSeparated Q.hom ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType Q.hom ∧ QuasiCompact Q.hom ∧ Flat q.left ∧ Surjective q.left ∧ (fst G H ≫ q = lift (fst G H) (snd G H ≫ i) ≫ μ[G] ≫ q) ∧ (∃ e : G ⊗ H ≅ pullback q q, e.hom ≫ pullback.fst q q = fst G H ∧ e.hom ≫ pullback.snd q q = lift (fst G H) (snd G H ≫ i) ≫ μ[G]) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of F))) (yoneda.obj Q) ∧ (∃ ηq : coequalizer (yoneda.map (fst G H)) (yoneda.map (lift (fst G H) (snd G H ≫ i) ≫ μ[G])) ⟶ yoneda.obj Q, coequalizer.π _ _ ≫ ηq = yoneda.map q ∧ ∀ Z : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of F))) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun f : yoneda.obj Q ⟶ Z.obj ↦ ηq ≫ f)) ∧ Function.Surjective (fun g : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of F))) ⟶ G ↦ g ≫ q) ∧ (∀ g₁ g₂ : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of F))) ⟶ G, g₁ ≫ q = g₂ ≫ q ↔ ∃ h : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of F))) ⟶ H, g₂ = g₁ * (h ≫ i))
lean.note: Two theorem statements cover the quotient and orbit clauses, respectively. The coset presheaf is the pointwise coequalizer of projection and right multiplication; its displayed arrow to the represented fppf sheaf satisfies exactly the sheafification universal property. The reduced orbit is characterized by its reduced locally closed immersion and exact topological image. Its isomorphism from any quotient presentation is unique with the stated orbit-map compatibility. No subgroup is assumed normal, reduced, smooth or connected.
